question: Who is known as the 'Grand Old Man of India' and promoted Indian economic nationalism?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Dadabhai Naoroji**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dadabhai Naoroji** is known as the **'Grand Old Man of India'** for his immense contributions to India's independence movement and economic thought.
 
• He was the first Indian to be elected as a Member of Parliament in the **British House of Commons** in 1892, representing the Liberal Party.
 
• Dadabhai Naoroji propagated the theory of **'Drain of Wealth'**, highlighting how British colonial rule exploited India's resources and wealth.
 
• He was a founding member of the **Indian National Congress (INC)** in 1885 and served as its president three times—in **1886, 1893, and 1906**.
 
• His book, **'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India'**, provided detailed evidence of economic exploitation under colonial rule and became a cornerstone of Indian economic nationalism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Lala Lajpat Rai**:

 
 
• Lala Lajpat Rai was an important freedom fighter known as **'Punjab Kesari'** or the 'Lion of Punjab'.
 
• He played a key role in the formation of the **Indian National Congress** and was a leader of the **Swadeshi Movement**.
 
• He is remembered for his protests against the Simon Commission in 1928, where he succumbed to injuries inflicted during a lathi charge.
 
 
 
• **Gopal Krishna Gokhale**:
 
 
• Gopal Krishna Gokhale was a senior leader of the Indian National Congress and a social reformer.
 
• He was a mentor to Mahatma Gandhi and emphasized **moderate political methods** for achieving independence.
 
• He founded the **Servants of India Society** in 1905 to promote education and social welfare.
 
 
 
• **Surendranath Banerjee**:
 
 
• Surendranath Banerjee was one of the earliest leaders of India's freedom struggle and a founder of the **Indian National Association** in 1876.
 
• He was known for his advocacy of **constitutional reforms** and moderate political methods.
 
• He also played a key role in the formation of the Indian National Congress.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Dadabhai Naoroji's Contributions:**

 
 
• He emphasized the need for self-rule and economic independence, forming the basis of Indian nationalism.
 
• His advocacy for Indians' representation in British administrative roles helped raise awareness about colonial exploitation.
 
• He was instrumental in creating a political awakening among Indians and advocating for their rights.
 
 
 
• **The Drain of Wealth Theory:**
 
 
• Dadabhai Naoroji argued that British policies resulted in the systematic extraction of India's resources and wealth.
 
• He identified factors such as excessive taxation, trade policies favoring Britain, and exploitation of Indian labor as causes of economic decline.
 
• This theory became a rallying point for Indian economic nationalism and self-rule demands.
